The core innovation lies in replacing Gaussian Process (GP) surrogates with Conformal Quantile Regression (CQR) surrogates within HPO pipelines. Unlike GP, which assumes homoskedastic Gaussian noise, CQR models heteroskedasticity directly via quantile regression and applies conformal corrections to yield valid uncertainty intervals. This allows GSI to maintain calibrated confidence even under variable noise regimes typical in real-world HPO. The resulting CQR surrogate offers superior calibration accuracy and computational efficiency compared to GP, especially at large sample sizes. In GSE, this translates into more reliable configuration selection and dynamic fidelity management. The last-fidelity aggregation simplifies multi-fidelity learning by treating each configuration as a single-fidelity observation at its final fidelity, avoiding complex joint models while still leveraging partial information. This enables asynchronous successive halving to prune poor performers efficiently. Expected improvement acquisition functions guide next-point selection based on surrogate estimates, incorporating fantasy sampling to account for pending evaluations. Together, these primitives form a robust, scalable, and theoretically grounded pipeline for optimizing black-box systems with uncertain outputs.

These developments culminate in modern automated machine learning frameworks like YAHPO and NAS-Bench.
